javax.microedition.theme
Class MediaObject

java.lang.Object
  javax.microedition.theme.MediaObject

public class MediaObject
extends java.lang.Object

Represents the media object content of an element. Media objects include bitmap and vector graphics, video clips and sound files. It must be possible to completely construct the binary media object from the data passed to this method.

All media objects have an associated media type, which is the IANA-registered MIME type of the media. Several different MIME types are sometimes used for the same media type, but the media type should be set to the most commonly used MIME type string for the media to improve interoperability. The format of all mediaType parameter values must conform to the MIME type syntax definition found in RFC 2045 (see reference [MIME]), and the type and subtype values should conform to the values in the IANA registry.

Constructor Detail

MediaObject

public MediaObject(java.lang.String mediaType,
                   byte[] data)

Constructs a media object with media type and binary data. The media type must be a MIME type string as described in the class description. The data array must contain the unadorned byte data that can be used to construct the media object.

Parameters:
mediaType - the media type string
data - the binary data for the media
Throws:
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if mediaType does not conform to the RFC 2045 syntax, or if the data array is empty

MediaObject

public MediaObject(java.lang.String mediaType,
                   java.io.InputStream in)
            throws java.io.IOException

Constructs a media object from an input stream. The input stream must be readable. The implementation must read all available data from the input stream, and may close the input stream after reading the data.

Parameters:
mediaType - the media type string
in - the input stream to read data from
Throws:
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if mediaType is the empty string
java.io.IOException - if there is an error reading data from the input stream
